title.narrative: Promoting awareness and advocacy of the human security approach as a strategy to address the current crisis in the Municipalities of Praia, São Filipe and São Vicente in Cabo Verde

description.narrative:
The scope of this programme is to promote awareness and advocacy on the relevance of the human security approach in the context of multiple crises experienced at the global, regional and national levels, at a time when there is a simultaneous step backwards for the development of the human development process, posing unprecedented challenges to humanity.
Cabo Verde, as Small Island Developing State (SIDS) and due to its own characteristics, has been particularly affected by the health, humanitarian and climate crises of recent times, deepening pre-existing economic, social and environmental vulnerabilities and limiting its sustainable development.
The first awareness raising programme on human security in Cabo Verde, funded by the UNTFHS, succeeded in bringing a renewed sense of hope to that fringe of the population benefiting from this approach, which was very fragile due to the deterioration of their living conditions, especially for those who were already in a situation of vulnerability before the recent events. However, the impact of the current crisis persists and constitute threats and challenges to the recovery and resilience building of the population, given the direct implications on the lives of Cabo Verdeans.
The programme will use the same interdisciplinary human security approach and methodology adopted to promote actions at the local level in order to increase the resilience and responses of vulnerable urban communities to the identified threats. This will be achieved through the participatory construction of community strategies that aim to promote sustainable livelihoods and economic opportunities, while improving access to basic social services and promoting a culture of peaceful coexistence.
The approach taken to public spaces in the original programme will be expanded to cover the integrality of social housing projects, which, although improving some aspects of the living conditions of their beneficiaries, often bear the consequences of the disruption of the social capital that beneficiaries had in their original settlement. At the same time, the programme will work to build the capacity of national and local actors to integrate the human security approach into national recovery and development plans through training, media campaigns and institutionalized frameworks for exchanging and sharing experiences on implementation. Furthermore, the communities that have already benefited from the programme will be monitored, with their experience being an important testimony to the dissemination of the results expected for new beneficiaries and the partners mobilization that is hoped for.
The program will be implemented jointly by UNODC and UN-Habitat in partnership with the Ministries of Justice (MJ), Infrastructure, Territorial Planning and Housing (MIOTH), Health (MS), the Municipalities of Praia (Santiago Island), São Filipe (Fogo Island) and Mindelo (São Vicente Island) and local NGOs.
The program will look for advice and input from the Human Security Unit in the human security integration and awareness tools to be developed at the community and municipal planning phase.
Please note UN-Habitat will lead Output 2.1 (Capacities of vulnerable communities and territorial actors of the three municipalities strengthened in the human security approach to contribute with recommendations to improving interventions and policies/strategies), including the following activities: • Activity 2.1.1 Expansion of the methodology developed and successfully tested for the previous programme, to incorporate now a social housing project analysis in its integrity. • Activity 2.1.2 Site-specific assessment in the three participating social housing projects to provide the baseline conditions for the application of the Block-by-Block approach and proposal for interventions. • Activity 2.1.3 Conduction of community workshops with the participation of city officials, following the Block by Block methodology, which includes Minecraft draft and final modelling, training session, facilitation of the workshop, provision of handouts and certificates, and reporting. • Activity 2.1.4 Translating the results of the community workshop sessions into proposals for interventions and enhanced policies/strategies and their validation by the community, as a key component of the human security approach in the vulnerable community.
Otherwise, UN-Habitat will support UNODC in the remaining outputs and activities.
